::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
renv::restore()
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the operating system, the installed system libraries and the network, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

CRAN only provides binaries for Windows and macOS, and only for recent package versions. On Linux, or for an old version frozen in a lockfile, R downloads the sources and compiles. Some packages then need system libraries (`libxml2`, `libcurl`, `gdal`...) along with their development files.

If they are missing, the compilation fails. The useful message, something like "configuration failed" or a header file that cannot be found, is buried in a long compilation log. The same lockfile works on a machine that already has those libraries.

## The remedy

Use a repository that serves Linux binaries (Posit Package Manager), and list the system dependencies to install.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://p3m.dev/cran/__linux__/noble/latest"))
renv::restore()
```

```bash
# for a given package, the list of system dependencies
Rscript -e 'pak::pkg_sysreqs("xml2")'
```
:::
